newsitem.title: URUGUAY: Narrow victory for change in Uruguay referendum.
newsitem.headline: Narrow victory for change in Uruguay referendum.

text.p: Uruguayans have voted narrowly in favour of changing their country's complex voting laws but the official result of Sunday's referendum will be declared after a recount, officials said on Monday.
In the referendum, 50.2 percent voted in favour of changing the constitution to forbid political parties from fielding more than one candidate in presidential elections.

The official electoral tribunal said that the narrow margin required a recount, which will take until the end of the month. Political analysts said that the vote for change would probably emerge as the winner.
The change to the constitution proposed by the referendum would also install a second round to presidential elections if no candidate received an absolute majority of votes in the first round.

Under current electoral rules, one political party can field several candidates in presidential elections. Its most sucessful candidate then gets the votes for all the other candidates of the same party added to his own tally.

Most of the big political parties, including the governing Colorado Party, supported changing the voting laws. But the leader of the leftist Frente Amplio, Tabare Vazquez, urged voters to block change.

The Ministry of the Interior said 979,000 voters had voted to change the constitution, while 905,000 voters were against it. But the lead by the "yes" votes narrowed to only 7,744 votes once blank and void voting tickets are added to the tally as required by Uruguayan law.
